Arhinful 18 November 2026 5:10pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Ranking Member on Parliament’s Finance Committee and former Finance Minister, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, has accused Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson of failing to account for jobs promised under the 2025 and 2026 budgets.
He said the 2027 Budget presented to Parliament did not provide any clear assessment of the employment commitments made in the previous two fiscal years, raising concerns about the government’s record on job creation.
Speaking during the parliamentary debate on the 2027 Budget, Dr Amin Adam said he had expected the Finance Minister to provide figures showing how many jobs had been created through the programmes announced in the previous budgets.
“2027 failed to account for jobs promised in both 2025 and 2026 budgets and the Finance Minister failed to give account of the jobs promised. Finance Minister couldn’t account for a single job that he promised in those two budgets,” he said.
He argued that the failure to provide an account of the government’s employment commitments undermined confidence in its job creation agenda, particularly at a time when many young Ghanaians were expecting concrete opportunities from the government’s economic programmes.
